pr_title: Respect controllers on PVCs for retention policy
pr_body:
/kind bug

Fixes #122400

/assign @msau42 

```release-note
StatefulSet autodelete will respect controlling owners on PVC claims as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4375
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

- [KEP #1847](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1847)

/ok-to-test

@atiratree it's ready to be reviewed now, thanks for you patience.

I changed updateClaimOwnerRefForSetAndPod to be more of a reconcilliation style (clear our refs out to a known state, then set them how they should be). This seemed to be the best way to deal with all the possible corner cases.  I think it addresses all your concerns.
@atiratree, any chance you can take another look at this? Thanks!

Thanks for the review! 

The push I just did contains all the responses to the comments --- I did them all, except the ones around validation + a couple more comments/questions.

The e2e test may not be passing, I'll check into that tomorrow.

The e2e test passed locally.

Note that the unknown controller ref still causes the pvc to be deleted. But that's on the controller semantics, not us; I verify in the test we don't update the controller.
Hmm, the e2e test are passing locally, but not in the CI. Investigating.
Hmm, something was strange in my e2e test logic. fiddling.

Ok, cleaned it up. I think the problem was accidentally looking for the unknown claim, along with a race condition on finding or not finding the first claim. It's passing locally, let's see what happens in the CI.

Uff, that was tricky.

I didn't realize that the stale owner ref would trigger the garbage collector on the PVC. When filtering the e2e run to just the single test, the GC doesn't get called, but when running in the presubmit it gets called much more frequently. So the behavior was different locally than in the presubmit.

I used a finalizer to pin the PVC with the stale ref so we can test the update behavior.

If the tests pass this should be good to review.

issue_context.title: StatefulSet Autodelete owner references should respect controller
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

StatefulSet owner references don't set or respect the controller flag.

That should either be used, preferably through controller-runtime/controllerutil as is used in controllers like RabbitMq, crunchy postgres and Neo4jCluster.

We have observed these controllers being used on stateful sets. We haven't seen any reports of controller contention problems but the potential is there.

This should delay GA promotion of the statefulset autodelete feature (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1847).

/assign @mattcary
/sig apps

comments: Hmm, I don't see controller-runtime used in k8s. What's in pkg/controller/controller_utils.go doesn't seem appropriate so I guess I'll just roll it manually.

review_comments: same here
ditto

- we should not test something that cannot be validated on admission
- we should test when one of them is not a controller and the other is

I'm not sure why admission validation affects the behavior we want to test for. This way we know we have consistent behavior even if something goes awry with validation.

+1 on testing variations on controller vs not controller.
ok, same as above, please at least write a comment on it here
done
can we remove the controller flag from one of the claims here and check it gets reconciled back to true?
Done
how come 1 is still there if the expectedExternalRef doesn't have the controller flag? Am I missing something?
An external owner ref is a stale owner ref, see stateful_set_utils.go:isClaimOwnerUpToDate.

I understand it better now. It reconciles normally and still has both refs: `slices.Concat(expectedExternalRef, expectedOwnerRef)`

It does not get deleted because of the first one. Unfortunately because we create a non-existent reference we fire the following errors in the KCM garbage collector:

```
E0501 00:27:21.573617  154898 garbagecollector.go:397] "error syncing item" err="unable to get REST mapping for unknown/v1/randomOwner." logger="garbage-collector-controller" item="[v1/PersistentVolumeClaim, namespace: statefulset-7724, name: datadir-ss-1, uid: 6f062806-1064-4df6-a6da-63c2cd3d7929]"
```

which I think is rather unfortunate, and it would be better if we could prevent that by creating an existing reference or at least an existing kind.

Oh, interesting. I wasn't looking at the errors in the controller-manager so missed that. I agree we want to reduce the noise.

I've changed it to use a config map which seems to have fixed it (also change another dummy kind).
+1. Can we also properly comment out why the PVCs are not getting deleted at the end?
done
can we simplify this and just do `DeepEqual`?

DeepEqual won't work if the order of the references changes?

Being order-independent will make the test less fragile and less of a change-detector.

No, it won't, but the order should be predictable so it should be fine in our test (it is used in other places in the codebase. I think it is preferable from a maintainability perspective, rather than adding another helper function.

It makes the test cases much harder to write, you have to remember the order-dependence. That makes it frustrating and time-consuming to make any update to the test.

Every time I've written or seen a test that depends on order, I've regretted it. The helper function IMHO makes maintainability much better.
Okay. In that case, I think it would be appropriate to have a unit test for the new function.
Good point, done.
Thanks

I am a bit bothered that this depends on claimOwnerMatchesSetAndPod working correctly. Can we handle stale controller owner references here as well and skip early? Maybe hasUnexpectedController could return multiple values on what kind of unexpected controller this is.

What I found when refactoring this is that it gets very confusing & hard to maintain if we try to combine update logic and validation logic.

I think it will be a lot more understandable and reliable to have the update code just update and the validation code (isClaimOwnerUpToDate) just validate. Otherwise we can get into many weird corner cases and hard to reason about code.
Ok, makes sense. Can we at least mention that `isClaimOwnerUpToDate` should be always called first before calling the `updateClaimOwnerRefForSetAndPod` in the function doc?

It's not necessary to call isClaimOwnerUpToDate first. After calling updateClaimOwnerRefForSetAndPod, usually the caller will make an api server update call which is potentially expensive, so calling isClaimOwnerUpToDate avoids that.

That seems to be the logic in stateful_set_control.go, eg see around line 442.

Yes. I know this is a nitpick, but I still think it would be useful to document this dependency as it is desirable to prevent the extra calls. Especially because the isClaimOwnerUpToDate is wrapped in ClaimsMatchRetentionPolicy.
Ok, done.
again validation
a comment in these place please
The test case name serves as the comment, I've clarified it.
samer UID issue here
Yes, this test case confirms that we report that as unexpected, as above?
Why do we need to match both statefulset and pod in the loop above?
PVC are controlled by the statefulset for the WhenDeleted retention type, and controlled by the pod for the WhenScaled retention type.
and here also a note that even inconsistent references with multiple owners will be cleaned up
Done, further down.

```suggestion
        // Need to adopt the claim as a controller.
		return false
```
done

>  Some other resource besides our set or pod has an owner ref

It seems that other resources do not necessarily have to be registered as owners in the references to get to this line. That is, it can be just one owner reference (e.g. our set or pod).
Done
I don't think this will pass the validation, so no need to test this.
seems cheap to leave it in though --- whatever validation is done is not very well documented at the least.
ok, can you please at least write a comment here that this should not pass the validation, but we are testing it regardless? So it does not surprise the next person reading it.
Done
thx
can we also test set references in these test cases?
Done
I don't understand why we should react in such a situation? It doesn't matter that we don't own it, and furthermore who owns it. We just don't react on it.
At most we can warn the user about such situation.

The implementation before this change makes statefulsets & pods owners but not controllers -- that's what this PR is fixing. So we have to handle at least that case to correctly update existing statefulsets from before this bugfix.
we should do a check of both set and pod references in case there are both at the same time to be sure - even though we do not set both at the same time
I'm not sure what you mean --- both set.GetUID & opd.GetUID are checked?

my original thought was:

> Suppose you have a list of owner references:
>
> `[{Kind: "Pod", Controller: nil}, {Kind: "StatefulSet", Controller: ptr.To(true)}]`
>
> If both of these match our set and pod UIDs, then the function will return early, even though we are the controller.


hm maybe I am confused by the name of the function and the fact there cannot be two controllers and it checks only some refs. 

No code change necessary, but maybe we could just name it better? What about `isMissingControllerFlag`?
This is checking that there is an owner that is not a controller -- a non-controller, as the function comment explains.
good, although it would be better to have it reflected in the function name as well
Done
Why not using `IsControlledBy` from `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1`

That matches on the UID, not on the GVK & name. So if, eg, the statefulset was updated, IsControlledBy won't return true until the UID is updated? In particular, matchRef is used to update stale UIDs.

If there is a StatefulSet with incorrect uid, then it means the old StatefulSet was deleted and its PVCs incorrectly orphaned.

This would suggest a mistake in the orphaning and it might be better to not to touch the PVC and report this as unexpected.
Yeah, that seems to be a good point, thanks.
